detailed_rationale:
Bajaj Auto's business momentum is genuinely strong right now, not manufactured. Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was Rs 16,006 crore (+32% YoY) with PAT of Rs 2,746 crore (+34% YoY, the highest ever for a single quarter); full-year FY26 standalone PAT was Rs 9,825 crore (+21%). June 2026 total volumes rose 28% YoY to 4,63,202 units - domestic up 11% (1,66,956 2W units) and exports up 47% (2,22,439 2W export units). For Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026), exports (7,32,173 units, +54% YoY) outsold domestic (7,06,078 units, +11% YoY) in absolute unit terms for effectively the first time - this is a volume-led export recovery, not a price/mix story: Latin America (~35% of exports - Colombia, Argentina, Brazil) and Africa (~30% - Nigeria, Uganda, Kenya) are rebounding as dollar/forex availability improves for African distributors after the 2023-24 currency crisis that had crushed the export book. Domestic growth is more modest and partly a GST base effect - the Sept 22, 2025 GST cut on sub-350cc 2W/3W (28%->18%) drove ex-showroom price cuts of Rs 5,000-24,500 that pulled demand forward into H1 FY27 rather than signalling a structural re-acceleration in domestic motorcycle demand.

Chetak (EV) has genuinely arrived: 23% of India's e2W market in June 2026 (43,234 units), a clear #2 behind TVS (25%, 46,999 units) and ahead of Ather (16%, nearly doubled YoY) and a declining Ola Electric (16,144 units, down from 20,697 a year ago, in a market that itself grew registrations 74% YoY). Cumulative Chetak sales crossed 8,00,085 units since Jan 2020 and management indicates the EV book has moved into double-digit EBITDA profitability from losses a year earlier - real structural progress, not a subsidy artefact. KTM is the bigger swing factor and the bigger risk. Bajaj completed its acquisition of a 74.9% controlling stake in Pierer Mobility AG (renamed Bajaj Mobility AG, effective Jan 13, 2026), paying roughly $58 million to complete the call option plus EUR 800 million cash to settle Pierer Mobility's creditors and restart production, alongside workforce cuts at KTM. The headline "consolidated PAT +103% YoY" in Q4 FY26 is flattered by a one-time fair-value/bargain-purchase gain of roughly Rs 1,195 crore from the November 2025 KTM consolidation - strip that out and the standalone PAT growth of +34% is the clean operating number. KTM's own CY2025 net profit of EUR 590 million was itself "supported by a restructuring gain of EUR 1,193 million" per its own results, so the KTM turnaround remains substantially a paper/accounting event at this stage; Bajaj management itself calls it "work in progress."

At CMP ~Rs 10,300 (mid-July 2026; 52-week range Rs 7,858.5-10,834; market cap ~Rs 2,84,137 crore), the stock trades near 27-29x trailing P/E and ~19x forward EV/EBITDA on FY26 estimates - a multiple that already presumes continued EV share defence, a durable (not merely cyclical) export recovery, and a clean KTM integration, none of which is guaranteed. Export growth is a rebound off a currency-crisis-driven trough and is guided by analysts toward ~20% in FY27 versus the 47-54% currently printing; the e2W field is only getting more contested (Ather nearly doubling units, Hero MotoCorp nearly tripling registrations YoY); and FY27 carries a genuine input-cost headwind - steel +~15%, copper +~20%, aluminium/PGMs +35-45%, adding an estimated 3.5-4% of revenue to costs, of which management's own guidance is that pricing/mix/currency actions offset only ~40%. Capital discipline is a real positive: the FY26 dividend (Rs 150/share) plus the Rs 5,633 crore buyback (record date June 24, 2026) return roughly 100% of standalone FY26 PAT to shareholders, but that is a payout story, not a re-rating catalyst. Q1 FY27 results are scheduled for board approval on July 21, 2026 and were NOT yet released as of this research (2026-07-19); the June 2026 monthly sales print and the export/EV share data above are already public and reflect the full quarter's volume trend ahead of the P&L release.
recommendation_rationale: Not because the underlying business is broken - standalone execution on volumes, EV mix and margins is genuinely good - but because the current price already assumes the good scenario continues on all three growth vectors simultaneously (export supercycle, EV share, KTM turnaround), and a meaningful slice of the reported consolidated growth rate (~Rs 1,195 crore, roughly 11% of FY26 consolidated PAT) is a one-off accounting gain rather than operating performance. Against a genuine forward blended growth estimate of ~13%, a 27-29x trailing multiple leaves very little room for any of the three legs (export deceleration already guided by the Street, intensifying EV competition, or a KTM turnaround that is still largely unrealised) to disappoint. This is a valuation call, not a business-quality call.
summary: Bajaj Auto had a genuinely strong FY26 - motorcycle exports to Africa and Latin America are recovering fast as currency conditions there normalise, and its Chetak electric scooter has become a real, profitable #2 player in India's EV two-wheeler market behind TVS. But the stock's price already reflects all of this good news and then some: it trades near 27-29 times last year's profit, a level that assumes the export rebound, the EV lead, and the newly acquired KTM motorcycle business in Austria all keep delivering without a hitch. About a tenth of last year's reported profit growth actually came from a one-time accounting gain tied to the KTM acquisition rather than from selling more vehicles, and rising steel, copper and aluminium costs will pressure margins this year. We rate it a Sell on valuation grounds - a genuinely good company, priced for a best-case outcome that leaves little room for any of its growth engines to slow down.
positive_para: Domestic 2W demand is steady with a genuine GST-cut tailwind still working through the system, and the export book is finally recovering in volume terms as African and Latin American currency/financing conditions normalise - Q1 FY27 export units (+54% YoY) now exceed domestic units for the first time. Chetak has won a durable #2 position in India's EV two-wheeler race (23% share) with genuine double-digit EBITDA profitability, not a subsidy-dependent number, while Ola Electric - once the category leader - is losing share outright. KTM gives Bajaj a global premium-motorcycle option once integration stabilises, and capital allocation discipline is strong: the FY26 dividend plus buyback return roughly 100% of standalone PAT to shareholders rather than chasing low-return growth. The captive NBFC, Bajaj Auto Credit (FY26 AUM Rs 18,450 crore, 17.89 lakh active customers), is a credible multi-year penetration and attach-margin lever still in its early scaling phase.
negative_para: The valuation already assumes all three growth engines keep compounding near current, currently-elevated rates - but each carries a natural deceleration or execution risk. Export growth is a rebound off a 2023-24 African-forex-crisis trough that analysts themselves guide to roughly halve (to ~20%) in FY27 from the 47-54% printing now; the EV field is getting more crowded, not less (Ather nearly doubled units YoY, Hero MotoCorp nearly tripled registrations, in a market still expanding 74% YoY); and roughly Rs 1,195 crore - about 11% - of FY26 consolidated PAT growth came from a one-time KTM bargain-purchase/restructuring gain rather than from operations, while KTM's own CY2025 profit was itself substantially a restructuring-gain artefact and management calls the turnaround "work in progress." Layer in a genuine FY27 input-cost headwind (~3.5-4% of revenue from steel/copper/aluminium, only ~40% offset by management's own admission) and a stock priced at 27-29x trailing earnings has very little margin of safety if even one of the three growth legs undershoots.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At 27-29x trailing P/E and ~19x forward EV/EBITDA, the market is pricing Bajaj to sustain low-to-high-teens consolidated earnings growth for several years running - a continuation of the current export-recovery pace (moderating only gently), further EV share gains with improving margins, and a smooth, real (not accounting-driven) KTM turnaround. My own forward view is a genuine blended ~13% revenue/earnings CAGR over 3-5 years: domestic ICE volumes are a mature, mid-single-digit growth story once the GST-cut demand pull-forward fades; export growth normalises from the current 47-54% print toward the ~20% the Street itself is guiding as the African/Latin American base normalises; Chetak keeps growing but into a more contested field (Ather, Hero, and new entrants scaling fast); and KTM's contribution is uncertain given its own turnaround remains substantially unrealised in operating terms. A genuine ~13% growth business does not comfortably clear a ~28x multiple over a 3-5 year horizon without further re-rating risk on any disappointment - on my own numbers the stock looks rich, not cheap.

technical_commentary: Clear 2021-2024 uptrend into a Rs11,874 peak, a real 36% top-to-bottom correction into early 2025, and since then a sustained, orderly recovery that has retraced most of the damage (now -19% off ATH vs. -36% at the trough). MA stack is fully bullish (price>10m>20m>40m) with clean, directional legs on each pullback-and-bounce rather than whipsaw. Still short of confirming new highs (only 2 of the last 24 months) -- a recovering trend, not yet a leading one.
